title: The Ways Between — Obishaal, the Realm of Dreams and Death
label: chap:ways-between
key_demographic: The dead, the dreaming, and those who trespass

overview.tagline: Every dream is a door. Every door is a judgment. The dead dream forever; the living borrow their sleep.
overview.genre: Dream-death metaphysical, virtue-based ascent, temptation and fall, folk-surrealism.
overview.mood: Obishaal — the Realm of Dreams and Death
overview.starting_location: A crossroad shrine of black glass stones, where travelers meet their reflections coming the other way. The shrine is silent except for the soft hum of the stones. A Backwards Pilgrim stands at the crossroads, facing the direction you came from. "The Thirteenth Stone speaks," they say. "But the path chooses who arrives. What did you bury on the road here? The stones can smell it. And in Obishaal, every buried thing dreams of waking."

lore.history: The Ways Between is a transit way, the eternal crossroads through Obishaal, the element of Dreams and Death, the eighth element after Fire, Life, Air, Fortune, Earth, Fate, Water, Dreams/Death. It is the realm where the settled dead go not to oblivion but to an ideal afterlife — a dream that reflects the life they lived. A farmer dreams of endless harvest; a warrior dreams of eternal battle; a merchant dreams of scales that never tip. These dreams are real, and they are paradise or prisons. The living may enter the Ways through thresholds of sleep, near-death, or deliberate ritual. Once inside, they find a landscape that shifts with their own psyche — but also with the weight of their choices. To ascend through the layers of Obishaal, a traveler must demonstrate virtue: honesty, courage, mercy, self-sacrifice. To fall is to yield to vice: greed, cowardice, cruelty, despair. Each layer is a test, and each test is a dream that tempts you to fail. At the very bottom, pressed into the silt of the deepest dream, lies Ikasha, She Who Sleeps. Her sisters Inaea and Isoka imprisoned her there eons ago, for Ikasha dreamed of summoning and confronting the Clockwork Monad — a confrontation that, in their judgment, would unmake reality. Now Ikasha dreams fitfully, and her nightmares seep upward, infecting the layers above. Sometimes a traveler who falls far enough can hear her voice, offering escape in exchange for service — a service that would free her. Between the layers drift the dead who have not yet found their final dream. They are the Unsettled, and they will trade memories, secrets, and virtues for a chance to ascend — or to pull you down with them.
lore.first_notice: The air tastes of copper and old keys. Your footsteps echo half a beat too late. The waystones are warm — and they pulse like hearts.
lore.rule_that_kills: Never answer a question asked by a reflection. The answer will bind you to the path you did not choose.

overview.regional_mood: Here, the dream is not a thing — it is a witness. It remembers every promise made at a deathbed, every lie told to a dying ear, every virtue you failed to keep. Obishaal does not forgive, but it does not forget either. It offers passage in exchange for truth. The longer you stay, the more the dream learns about you. By the time you reach your destination, you may find that the destination knows you better than you know yourself. Some travelers never leave. They become dream-echoes, their faces pressed into the glass of a forgotten dream, their names still warm on the lips of the next pilgrim.

regional_diagnostic.current_hook: Every dream is a door. Every door is a judgment. The dead dream forever; the living borrow their sleep.
regional_diagnostic.core_conflict: Travelers must demonstrate virtue to ascend through Obishaal's layers or yield to vice and fall — and at the bottom, the imprisoned dreaming goddess Ikasha whispers bargains to those who fall far enough.
regional_diagnostic.unique_feature: **Virtue and Vice Timers:** each character in Obishaal tracks a personal Virtue [3] and Vice [3] timer; filling one causes ascension (a boon) or a fall (a temptation), resetting after each layer transition.
regional_diagnostic.ninth_taboo: On any path in the Ways Between, the ninth step you take in a straight line will land on a threshold you did not see. The wise take eight steps, then pause to look around. In Obishaal, the ninth step is always a dream of falling. Those who fall hear a voice ask, 'What did you owe?' Answering costs a memory; silence costs a name.

quotes.speaker: The Wayfinder (Elite)
quotes.text: I exist only in the moment of choice, the breath between one path and another. Obishaal is not a place — it is a state. To guide here is to understand that every dream leads somewhere, but only the virtuous know which somewhere is worth the waking.

quotes.speaker: Lost Pilgrim (Commoner)
quotes.text: The dead don't leave. They just change addresses. Obishaal is their new neighborhood, and the scales are balanced with virtue. If you're lucky, you'll only visit. If you're not… you'll find yourself climbing stairs that never end, and every landing offers a bargain you can't refuse.

thin_places.description: Not every threshold is a door. Some are a crack — a place where the world forgot to finish its seam. The Pereshi call them breath-holes, where the mountain's exhalation smells of yesterday. The Tulkani knot a thread and leave it untied, marking where the Hollow's attention wanders. The Aeler do not name them at all. They simply count to eight and leave the ninth breath unspoken. A thin place is a location where the boundary between the waking world and the Ways Between is unusually permeable. Crossing is not a matter of ritual or intent — it is a matter of being in the wrong place at the wrong angle. A wrong step. A miscounted breath. A name spoken at the wrong hour.
when_a_thin_place_opens: A character rolls a critical failure (all 1s) on a navigation or survival test in a liminal region (Valewood, Mistlands, high passes, deep mines, ancient ruins).
The party camps at a crossroads, bridge, or ford during a new moon, an eclipse, or the ninth hour.
A character breaks a taboo (pours the ninth cup, takes the ninth step, speaks the ninth name) in a region where the Hollow is strong.
The GM spends 3+ Story Beats to introduce a supernatural complication, and the fiction supports a threshold crossing.
A player willingly seeks a thin place (rare — most who seek them never return unchanged).
signs_of_a_thin_place_d6: Echoes answer wrong. Your voice returns half a heartbeat later, or in a different pitch. Sometimes the echo speaks words you did not say.
Shadows drift. Your shadow moves when you stand still. Cast by a light source that isn't there.
The ninth step appears. A stair, a bridge plank, a stone — where no ninth should exist. Step on it, and the ground shifts.
Bells ring without clappers. A distant chime, a temple bell, a levee alarm. The sound comes from a direction you cannot find.
The air tastes of copper and old keys. The same taste before every exorcism. The same taste named 'breath of the deep.'
A door stands where no door stood. Gray wood, warm handle, no frame. It does not open for those who knock. It opens for those who do not.
thin_places.accidental_crossing_mechanics: When a character is in a thin place and the conditions align, the GM may call for a Spirit + Resolve test (DV 4–6, depending on the thinness). On a failure, the character crosses into the Ways Between — not by choice, but by accident. **Partial success:** the character feels the pull; they may step back (mark 1 Fatigue) or let themselves cross (gain 1 Boon, but enter the Ways). **Miss:** the character crosses involuntarily, arriving at a random location (see accidental crossing destinations). **Critical failure:** the character crosses — and something crosses with them: an Oath-Keeper, a Counting Wraith, or worse. Once crossed, the character must navigate the Ways Between using standard travel procedures. They cannot simply 'turn back' — the threshold that opened may close behind them. Finding the way home requires a balance: a story, a memory, or a name offered to the road.

known_thin_places_by_region.hazard: The Bell-Crypts. Bells ring without clappers. A ninth tone pulls listeners into a dream-echo of the mountain's first collapse.
The Ninth Plank. Step where the plank is missing, and you step into the fog of Obishaal. The Hollow Bride sometimes waits on the far side.
The Star-Road Scar. Where the grass grows in spirals. Crossing at dusk may lead to the Long Mile of Temptation.
The Crack of the Ninth Clause. Touch the stone's newest crack, and you may hear the Oath-Keeper's question before you answer.
The Beacon That Remembers. When the beacon burns green, the dead can see you. When it burns blue, they can touch you.
The Ninth Flight. Climb where no stair should be, and you climb through the fossil stairs of Obishaal.
The Causeway of Broken Promises. Every milestone is a broken oath. Walk it at dusk, and the Walking Scale may find you.
The Hall of Shattered Mirrors. Mirrors show not your face, but a reflection of the path you refused.
The Queen's Milestone. The stone is cracked. The crack is a door. Those who peer inside see the Bone Corridor of Unfinished Business.
The Spire's Shadow. When the spire phases, its shadow becomes a stair. Climb it, and you enter the Stone Circle of Forgotten Villages.
The Gate That Expects Change. If you cannot pay the toll in truths, the gate may open to the Memory Tunnel of the Dying instead of the forest.
The Field of Uncounted Steps. Step nine times in a straight line, and the Hollow Field becomes the Mist-Ford of First Doubt.
The Reef That Sings. The harmonic hum is the song of the Deep Drake. Follow it, and you may find the Pressure's lair — or the Thirteenth Stone.
The Dreamer's Threshold. A cave that smells of honey and rust. Entering it is already a crossing. The Wayfinder waits inside.
The Well of Forgotten Names. Drink from it, and you may wake in the Waystation of the Virtuous, your name already spent.
The Coast of Unmarked Graves. The drowned walk here. If you answer a drowned sailor's question, you follow them into the Promise Bridge of the Unsettled.
The Stone That Asks. Touch it, and the mountain asks a question. Answer poorly, and you climb the Fossil Stairs of Ascension.
The Throne of Tails. The saddle has no stirrups. Sit in it, and the Long Mile of Temptation begins beneath you.
The Sealed Door. The stone is warm. The lock is a whisper. Those who listen too long cross into the deepest layer — and may never wake.
The City That Never Stopped. A walking city seen only on the horizon. Step onto its shadow, and you step into the Spiral Path of Recursion.
The Tomb of the Unnamed. The keystone is a door. The door leads to the Threshold Arch of Virtue. The arch judges.
The Root That Whispers. Sit on the throne of roots, and the tree asks one question. If you cannot answer, you fall into the Bone Corridor.
The Invisible Strand. Only those who have witnessed nine true oaths can see it. Cross it, and you walk the Promise Bridge of the Unsettled.
The Cliff of Nine Views. From here you can see the Green Host riding — and sometimes the Fossil Stairs rising beside them.
The Vault of Unpaid Scales. The records are warm. Read the ninth page, and the Thirteenth Stone speaks to you.
The Ferryman's Slip. The river is a threshold. Bryn's boat is not the only one. On moonless nights, the dead row themselves. A coin in the water may buy a crossing — or sell your name.

denizens.price_to_banish: A memory of sunlight (or a copper bell)
A true name carved in quartz

denizens.creature: The Keeper of the Seventh Exhalation

accidental_crossing_destinations_d6: The Mist-Ford of First Doubt (Class III Procession site). Water runs uphill. Footsteps echo backwards. The dead march here at midnight.
The Bone Corridor of Unfinished Business (Anchor graveyard). Shadows walk the walls but never touch the floor. A Poltergeist may be forming.
The Crossroads of the Ninth Choice (Threshold nexus). All four paths lead to the same destination — but different yesterdays. A Trow sits at the center, smoking.
The Promise Bridge of the Unsettled (Oath-Keeper territory). Cross with a vow, and the bridge remembers. The toll is a story you have never told.
The Long Mile of Temptation (Vice's testing ground). The road stretches differently for each traveler. A Walking Scale appears at the halfway mark.
The Thirteenth Stone (Ikasha's Seal). The path ends at a warm stone. The stone whispers. Beneath it, She Who Sleeps dreams of freedom. A Deep Drake may be coiled nearby.
thin_places.gm_guidance: Thin places are not traps. They are complications. A party that accidentally crosses into the Ways Between should not feel that they have 'failed.' They have simply entered a different kind of scene — one where negotiation matters more than steel. Offer a way out: the Ways Between always offer a path home, though the path may demand a toll (a memory, a story, a name). Use the travel rules: treat the Ways Between as a leg of a journey, draw cards, set timers. Let players use their bonds: a character who calls on a bond while lost may hear a familiar voice or see a familiar face guiding them. The ninth is always watching: in any scene set in the Ways Between, the ninth card drawn (or the ninth roll made) triggers a manifestation of the Hollow — not a fight, a question. The players must answer truthfully, or the road takes a memory. Set down by the Gray Wanderer, after a night spent in a thin place near the Black River. The fire went out three times. The shadows did not. The ninth bell rang once — and then was silent. The Ways Between are not a dungeon. They are a conversation. Speak carefully. The road listens.

places.title: Mist-Ford of First Doubt
places.subtitle: [THRESHOLD]
places.description: Water runs uphill; footsteps echo backwards through time.
places.flavor: The ford shows you wading through your own past. Do not look down at the water.
places.mechanical_hook: Crossing requires a Spirit or Resolve roll (DV 4); a Miss forces the character to relive a past failure as a brief, disorienting vision.

places.title: Bone Corridor of Unfinished Business
places.subtitle: [DEATH]
places.description: Shadows walk the walls but never touch the floor; light as memory.
places.flavor: The bones are from those who chose vice and fell. They shift when you blink.
places.mechanical_hook: Lingering here ticks the character's Vice timer by 1 unless they perform a genuine act of closure for one of the shadows.

places.title: Threshold Arch of Virtue
places.subtitle: [TRUTH]
places.description: Shows a reflection as someone you might have been; the past as a mirror.
places.flavor: The reflection has a scar you never got. It asks how you avoided it.
places.mechanical_hook: Answering the reflection honestly ticks Virtue by 1; lying ticks Vice by 1 instead — the arch always knows which.

places.title: Spiral Path of Recursion
places.subtitle: [MAGIC]
places.description: Ascends but returns to the same stone marker; the journey as meditation.
places.flavor: Each loop, the stone moves closer to the center. Or you do.
places.mechanical_hook: Escaping the loop requires a Wits+Lore roll (DV 5) or a genuine moment of self-reflection role-played at the table.

places.title: Promise Bridge of the Unsettled
places.subtitle: [OATH]
places.description: Cross with a vow and it remembers your weight; an oath as a toll.
places.flavor: The bridge's planks are old letters. Read one, and you may owe the writer.
places.mechanical_hook: Crossing requires naming an oath aloud; breaking that oath later automatically ticks the character's Vice timer.

places.title: Crossroads of the Ninth Choice
places.subtitle: [THRESHOLD]
places.description: All four paths lead to the same destination, but different tomorrows.
places.flavor: The center stone is warm. A coin placed there will vanish — or be accepted.
places.mechanical_hook: Choosing a path here is purely narrative — the GM should let the choice reflect the character's virtue/vice leaning rather than mechanical outcome.

places.title: Stone Circle of Forgotten Villages
places.subtitle: [DEATH]
places.description: Marks where a village used to be; the houses are now constellations.
places.flavor: The stars are too close. You can touch them. They crumble like ash.
places.mechanical_hook: Touching a star grants a fragment of lost regional history (GM's choice) but ticks a relevant Memory Currency cost.

places.title: Memory Tunnel of the Dying
places.subtitle: [MEMORY]
places.description: Hear the thoughts of those who passed here; the past as an echo.
places.flavor: The thoughts are in a language you almost understand. One word is your name.
places.mechanical_hook: Listening grants a genuine clue relevant to the current plot, but the character must resist (Resolve DV 4) or lose a minor personal memory.

places.title: Fossil Stairs of Ascension
places.subtitle: [FEAR]
places.description: Each step is an eye that watches your ascent; the climb as scrutiny.
places.flavor: The eyes belong to those who fell here. They blink in sequence.
places.mechanical_hook: Climbing under scrutiny requires a Resolve roll (DV 5) each landing; failure ticks Vice by 1 (fear curdling into despair).

places.title: Waystation of the Virtuous
places.subtitle: [SOCIAL]
places.description: The keeper trades in unfinished conversations; words as currency.
places.flavor: The keeper has no face. It wears the faces of those who paused too long.
places.mechanical_hook: Finishing an unfinished conversation (real or symbolic) with the keeper heals 1 Fatigue and ticks Virtue by 1.

places.title: Junction of Vice and Virtue
places.subtitle: [THRESHOLD]
places.description: Paths physically collide; you must choose which reality to follow.
places.flavor: The collision sounds like breaking glass. The glass reforms into a door.
places.mechanical_hook: The choice made here directly ticks either the Virtue or Vice timer by 1, decided by genuine player choice, not a roll.

places.title: Long Mile of Temptation
places.subtitle: [MAGIC]
places.description: The road stretches differently for each traveler; distance as perception.
places.flavor: You are the only one walking. The others are already at the end.
places.mechanical_hook: A Walking Scale appears at the halfway mark, testing a broken promise; resisting its temptation ticks Virtue, yielding ticks Vice.

places.title: The Thirteenth Stone — Ikasha's Seal
places.subtitle: [TRUTH]
places.description: Where the path reveals its true destination; truth as revelation.
places.flavor: The stone whispers. The whisper is a promise you made to yourself and broke. Beneath it, the stone is warm — and dreaming.
places.mechanical_hook: A character with a filled Vice timer who reaches this card may hear Ikasha's Whisper directly (see Additional Features).

people_and_factions.title: Lost Pilgrim
people_and_factions.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
people_and_factions.description: Thinks they're going home but forgot where; destination as a memory.
people_and_factions.flavor: Their pack is full of stones. Each stone is a forgotten promise.
people_and_factions.debt: They'll share a genuine piece of wisdom about the road ahead, if treated with patience.
people_and_factions.price: A memory of home, freely given, to help them remember theirs.

people_and_factions.title: Toll-Taker (Virtue Assessor)
people_and_factions.subtitle: [SOCIAL]
people_and_factions.description: Accepts payment in virtues you didn't know you had.
people_and_factions.flavor: Their scales weigh truth and echo. A balanced scale means you pass — for now.
people_and_factions.debt: They'll grant safe passage past a threshold, once, for a genuine act of virtue witnessed.
people_and_factions.price: An honest accounting of a recent choice, good or bad.

people_and_factions.title: Wayward Guide
people_and_factions.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
people_and_factions.flavor: They point with a broken compass. The needle spins, but the path is true.
people_and_factions.debt: They'll guide the party to their destination, technically correctly, once.
people_and_factions.price: Willingness to accept the guide's morally ambiguous shortcuts.

people_and_factions.title: Dream-Merchant
people_and_factions.subtitle: [MAGIC]
people_and_factions.description: Carries a sack of nightmares and one perfect dream for sale.
people_and_factions.flavor: The perfect dream is their own. They are selling it because they cannot wake up.
people_and_factions.debt: They'll sell a dream-fragment granting insight into a sleeping NPC's true motives.
people_and_factions.price: A memory or a promise, traded fairly.

people_and_factions.title: Child-Ghost of Unfinished Life
people_and_factions.subtitle: [DEATH]
people_and_factions.description: Knows shortcuts but charges in riddles; wisdom as a puzzle.
people_and_factions.flavor: The riddles have no answer — only a choice. Choose wrong, and you become a child.
people_and_factions.debt: They'll reveal a genuine shortcut through the Ways, if their riddle is answered honestly.
people_and_factions.price: A choice, made and stood by, even if the answer seems wrong.

people_and_factions.title: Wounded Walker (Vice-Bound)
people_and_factions.subtitle: [FEAR]
people_and_factions.description: Bleeding metaphor; their pain grows thorns along the path.
people_and_factions.flavor: The thorns have faces. Each face is someone they failed to save.
people_and_factions.debt: Helping them face one of the thorn-faces ticks the helper's Virtue by 1.
people_and_factions.price: Willingness to hear their story of failure in full.

people_and_factions.title: Map-Merchant of Impossible Dreams
people_and_factions.subtitle: [TRUTH]
people_and_factions.description: Selling maps to places that don't exist yet; the future as a commodity.
people_and_factions.flavor: The maps change as you watch. The destination is always one page ahead.
people_and_factions.debt: They'll sell a map to a future destination, genuinely useful but never quite complete.
people_and_factions.price: A memory of a place the party has actually been.

people_and_factions.title: Guide-Dog (Ancestral Spirit)
people_and_factions.subtitle: [SPIRIT]
people_and_factions.description: Made of shadow and starlight; follows those who walk with purpose.
people_and_factions.flavor: It never barks. It whines when you are about to make a mistake.
people_and_factions.debt: It will silently warn the party of an impending mistake, once, if they walk with genuine purpose.
people_and_factions.price: No price — it simply requires sincerity of intent to stay nearby.

people_and_factions.title: Backwards Pilgrim (Dream-Echo)
people_and_factions.subtitle: [MEMORY]
people_and_factions.description: Moving through time; their steps erase what just happened.
people_and_factions.flavor: They are walking toward their birth. Every step, they forget something.
people_and_factions.debt: They can be asked one question about the past, answered with fading but genuine clarity.
people_and_factions.price: Watching them forget something in exchange for the answer.

people_and_factions.title: Soul-Ferryman
people_and_factions.subtitle: [DEATH]
people_and_factions.description: Carries the luggage of the living; a burden as a service.
people_and_factions.flavor: The luggage is full of things you never said. The ferryman knows them all.
people_and_factions.debt: He'll carry an unspoken burden for the party for one crossing, symbolically clearing a Condition.
people_and_factions.price: Speaking the unsaid thing aloud, at least once, to him.

people_and_factions.title: Road's Child (Dream-Kin)
people_and_factions.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
people_and_factions.description: Born where paths crossed, raised by waymarks; navigation as instinct.
people_and_factions.flavor: They have no navel. They were never born — they simply began.
people_and_factions.debt: They'll navigate any path in Obishaal instinctively, granting +1 die to the next navigation roll.
people_and_factions.price: Genuine curiosity and respect for their strange nature — they dislike being treated as a tool.

people_and_factions.title: Dead-Road Keeper
people_and_factions.subtitle: [DEATH]
people_and_factions.description: Ensures proper passage for those who should not walk.
people_and_factions.flavor: Their lantern burns a cold blue. The flame does not flicker.
people_and_factions.debt: They'll grant safe passage through a forbidden path, once, for those who should not walk it.
people_and_factions.price: A promise to eventually walk the path properly, when the time comes.

people_and_factions.title: The Wayfinder (Dream Avatar)
people_and_factions.subtitle: [LEGEND]
people_and_factions.description: Exists only in the moment a choice is made; a decision as an entity.
people_and_factions.flavor: They are every guide you ever needed. They are also every road you refused.
people_and_factions.debt: They appear only at the moment of a genuinely difficult choice, offering clarity — never an answer.
people_and_factions.price: The choice, once made, is binding and cannot be undone by mechanical means.

complications.title: Funeral Loop
complications.subtitle: [DEATH] [FEAR]
complications.description: The path shows your funeral preparations; death as a destination.
complications.flavor: The mourners are people you have not met yet. They seem to know you well.
complications.mechanical_hook: Witnessing your own funeral forces a Resolve roll (DV 4); failure ticks Vice by 1 (despair).

complications.title: Reality Thins (Ikasha's Dream Bleed)
complications.subtitle: [MAGIC]
complications.description: You see the dreams of sleeping travelers; the boundary as a veil.
complications.flavor: A dreamer mutters your name. They are dreaming of a choice you will make tomorrow.
complications.mechanical_hook: The GM may offer a genuine piece of foreshadowing about an upcoming decision, at the cost of unsettling the character (mark 1 Fatigue).

complications.title: Waymark Lies (Vice's Test)
complications.subtitle: [TRUTH]
complications.description: Points the wrong way; trust leads to places that never were.
complications.flavor: The waymark has a crack. Through the crack, you see a path you should have taken.
complications.mechanical_hook: Following the waymark without verifying (Wits+Lore, DV 4) leads the party one segment off course on their journey timer.

complications.title: Dream-Bleed
complications.subtitle: [MEMORY] [FEAR]
complications.description: Waking memories become someone else's nightmares.
complications.flavor: You remember a childhood fear that was not yours. It still terrifies you.
complications.mechanical_hook: The character gains a temporary Condition (Borrowed Fear) until they identify whose memory it was and return it symbolically.

complications.title: Toll Demanded (Virtue Payment)
complications.subtitle: [SOCIAL] [WEIGHT]
complications.description: Currency you did not know you carried; payment as a revelation.
complications.flavor: The toll is a secret you told a dead person. They are now standing behind you.
complications.mechanical_hook: Paying the toll (revealing the secret) ticks Virtue by 1 if honestly given; refusing ticks Vice by 1 and costs 1 Fatigue instead.

complications.title: Path Split (Virtue vs. Vice)
complications.subtitle: [MAGIC]
complications.description: Each version of you remembers differently; identity as a choice.
complications.flavor: One you is smiling. One you is weeping. One you is already walking away.
complications.mechanical_hook: The character must choose which reflection to follow — a purely narrative choice that the GM should tie to their current Virtue/Vice standing.

complications.title: Gravity Shifts (Guilt's Weight)
complications.subtitle: [WEATHER]
complications.description: Emotional weight grows physically heavy; a burden as physics.
complications.flavor: Your pack feels heavier. Inside is a regret you forgot you carried.
complications.mechanical_hook: Movement is Desperate until the regret is named aloud and set down (narratively resolved).

complications.title: Time-Sickness (Dream Chronology)
complications.subtitle: [MAGIC]
complications.description: You arrive before you left; paradox shadows follow.
complications.flavor: Your past self waves at you. Do not wave back.
complications.mechanical_hook: Interacting with the paradox self forces a Resolve roll (DV 5) or the character loses a segment of continuity on their travel timer (arriving later than expected).

complications.title: Truth Payment (Ikasha's Price)
complications.subtitle: [TRUTH] [WEIGHT]
complications.description: The road remembers your lies and demands truth as payment.
complications.flavor: The lie is carved on a stone. The stone is warm. It knows your temperature.
complications.mechanical_hook: The character must confess a genuine lie (in-fiction) to proceed; refusing bars passage entirely until they do.

complications.title: Crossroads Judgment (Virtue Audit)
complications.subtitle: [TRUTH] [SOCIAL]
complications.description: The path you chose judges the ones you did not; decision as karma.
complications.flavor: A ghost of the road not taken asks why. You have one sentence to answer.
complications.mechanical_hook: A single-sentence, in-character justification determines whether Virtue or Vice ticks by 1 — the GM judges sincerity, not cleverness.

complications.title: Memory-Thief (Unsettled Dead)
complications.subtitle: [MEMORY] [SOCIAL]
complications.description: A rest stop keeper pays in counterfeit recollections.
complications.flavor: The memory is almost right. The color of the sky is wrong.
complications.mechanical_hook: Accepting the counterfeit memory grants a temporary Boon but plants a false detail the GM may exploit later.

complications.title: Forbidden Path (Ikasha's Descent)
complications.subtitle: [DEATH]
complications.description: Opens only for those already lost; loss as a key.
complications.flavor: The path smells of old tears. You taste salt on your lips.
complications.mechanical_hook: Only a character with a filled Vice timer may enter this path; others find it simply will not open for them.

complications.title: Convergence (Ikasha's Waking)
complications.subtitle: [MAGIC] [LEGEND]
complications.description: All travelers arrive together, none recall how; arrival as a mystery.
complications.flavor: You recognize everyone. You have never seen any of them before. The air tastes of honey and rust. Ikasha is dreaming of you.
complications.mechanical_hook: Every NPC met previously in the Ways Between may reappear in this scene simultaneously — a major narrative convergence, GM's discretion on stakes.

rewards.title: Choice Compass (Virtue's Needle)
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
rewards.description: Always points toward your next important choice.
rewards.flavor: The needle is a splinter of the Thirteenth Stone. It hums when you are near a decision.
rewards.curse_cost: The compass only points toward choices — it never indicates which option is correct, only that one is coming.

rewards.title: Passage Token (Dream-Marked)
rewards.subtitle: [SOCIAL]
rewards.description: The road recognizes you as one who belongs.
rewards.flavor: The token is a braid of your own hair. You do not remember cutting it.
rewards.curse_cost: The token marks its holder as permanently known to the road — anonymity in Obishaal becomes impossible while it's carried.

rewards.title: Dream-Catcher
rewards.subtitle: [MAGIC]
rewards.description: Filters nightmares from your rest; sleep as a sanctuary.
rewards.flavor: The catcher is woven from old promises. It smells of lavender and regret.
rewards.curse_cost: The filtered nightmares don't disappear — they collect in the catcher, which grows heavier and darker over time.

rewards.title: Truth-Compass (Ikasha's Fragment)
rewards.subtitle: [TRUTH]
rewards.description: Points to what you most need to know, not what you want.
rewards.flavor: The compass has no needle. The housing spins until you speak a truth.
rewards.curse_cost: It only responds to genuine truths spoken aloud — flattery or convenient half-truths leave it spinning uselessly.

rewards.title: Memory-Anchor
rewards.subtitle: [MEMORY]
rewards.description: Keeps you from losing yourself on deeper paths.
rewards.flavor: The anchor is a river stone. Your name is carved on it in a language you have never seen.
rewards.curse_cost: Losing the anchor while deep in Obishaal risks the character forgetting their own name until it's recovered.

rewards.title: Safe Haven (Virtue's Rest)
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
rewards.description: A guaranteed rest stop without complication.
rewards.flavor: The haven is a dry arch. The arch is a doorframe with no door.
rewards.curse_cost: The haven can only be used once — trying to return to the same one a second time finds it empty and ordinary.

rewards.title: Guide-Light (Virtue's Beacon)
rewards.subtitle: [SOCIAL]
rewards.description: Burns the color of your truest intention; purpose as a beacon.
rewards.flavor: The light is blue. Blue means you are honest. Red means you are not.
rewards.curse_cost: The light is visible to everyone nearby, including hostile denizens — it cannot be hidden or dimmed.

rewards.title: Path-Cutter (Dream Shears)
rewards.subtitle: [MAGIC]
rewards.description: Cuts distance through metaphor, not space.
rewards.flavor: The cutter is a pair of shears. Cut a memory, and the road between here and there vanishes.
rewards.curse_cost: Each use permanently removes a memory from the wielder — chosen by the GM, not the player.

rewards.title: Scale-Clearing (Virtue's Mercy)
rewards.subtitle: [WEIGHT]
rewards.description: The road forgives one weight you thought you carried.
rewards.flavor: The weight was owed to a dead person. They are no longer dead on this path.
rewards.curse_cost: The forgiven debt's original holder may reappear later, expecting the forgiveness to be reciprocated in kind.

rewards.title: Crossroads Boon
rewards.subtitle: [LEGEND]
rewards.description: Choose among three paths, each exactly where you need to be.
rewards.flavor: The paths are labeled: Regret, Forgive, Forget. Choose carefully.
rewards.curse_cost: Whichever path is not chosen is lost forever — the other two options vanish once one is taken.

rewards.title: Way-Wisdom (Dream-Logic)
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
rewards.description: Understand the language of paths and signs for one journey.
rewards.flavor: The waystones whisper. They are complaining about the last traveler. It was you.
rewards.curse_cost: The understanding fades at the end of the journey, and the waystones remember the granting — they'll expect payment again next time.

rewards.title: Grace Passage (Virtue's Shield)
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
rewards.description: Walk safely through any dangerous crossing for one night.
rewards.flavor: The grace is a bell. Ring it, and the road will pretend not to see you.
rewards.curse_cost: The bell can only be rung once — and its silence afterward is conspicuous to anything still listening.

rewards.title: Road's Name (Ikasha's True Name)
rewards.subtitle: [LEGEND]
rewards.description: Call the path by its true name and command its nature.
rewards.flavor: The name is a single syllable. Speaking it will change the road — and you.
rewards.curse_cost: Speaking the name changes the speaker as much as the road — the exact nature of that change is the GM's to decide, and it is permanent.

quick_use_notes.draw_rules: Draw until you have all four suits: Spade = place, Heart = actor, Club = pressure, Diamond = leverage. Highest rank sets the main Timer (2–5 → 4, 6–10 → 6, J/Q/K → 8, A → 10).
quick_use_notes.diamonds: Diamonds are codified outcomes (true names/safe passages/waywisdom) that change position rather than call for a roll.
quick_use_notes.ace_rule: If any Ace appears, echo dream-road motifs — reflections that lie, paths that judge, destinations that choose the traveler. Also, the presence of an Ace hints that Ikasha's dream is particularly close.

additional_features.dream_logic_navigation: Any Ace introduces a metaphysical requirement (a sacrifice, a taboo, an exchange) that must be satisfied to pass. Name it at the table; the road will enforce it.
additional_features.reflection_points: Face cards (J, Q, K) show alternate selves or unlived choices. Treat them as temporary NPCs or scene tags that can help, hinder, or tempt.
additional_features.memory_currency: Diamonds may be traded for knowledge or safe passage as if they were memories. Describe the memory paid; the path (or its keeper) pays in kind.
additional_features.virtue_and_vice_timers: Each character in Obishaal tracks a small personal Virtue [3] and Vice [3] timer. Virtue advances when they act with honesty, courage, mercy, or self-sacrifice. Vice advances when they act with greed, cowardice, cruelty, or despair. When one timer fills, the character ascends (Virtue) to a higher layer of Obishaal or falls (Vice) to a lower one. Ascension offers a boon; falling offers a temptation (a cursed gift from the layer's vice-spirit). The timers reset after each layer transition. Reaching the bottom (Vice filled in the deepest layer) allows Ikasha to speak directly to the character.
additional_features.ikashas_whisper: When a character falls to the lowest layer (or deliberately seeks her out), they may hear Ikasha's voice. She offers a Fragment of Freedom: +2 dice to any roll involving escape, secrecy, or breaking bonds, but each use marks 1 Obligation to Ikasha and advances a Waking Dream [6] timer. When that timer fills, Ikasha uses the character as a vessel to attempt an escape — a campaign-level event.

local_patrons.name: The Unnamed Guide
local_patrons.description: The road that appears only when you are lost.

local_patrons.name: The Mirror Listener
local_patrons.description: The reflection that tells you what you need to hear, never what you want.

local_patrons.name: The Threshold Child
local_patrons.description: The one who was never born, who guards the places where paths end.

local_patrons.name: The Echo King
local_patrons.description: The voice that answers when you speak to the empty road.

local_patrons.name: The Dreamer Below
local_patrons.description: She who sleeps and dreams of waking. Her whispers are bargains; her freedom is a promise.

lore_echoes.title: The Bitter Root
lore_echoes.description: Daughters of the Cord know the Ways Between as the Cord's shadow. A lost Hollowed wanders here, its thread trailing into the mist. Follow it, and you may find a Sister who cut herself free — and who now tends Ikasha's dream.

lore_echoes.title: The Threshold Compendium
lore_echoes.description: Saikou Ira's silver mirror shows the Ways Between as a tangled knot of unfulfilled balances. He has walked three paths here. He will not speak of the fourth, where he glimpsed Ikasha's face.

lore_echoes.title: Malachai, the Chained Angel
lore_echoes.description: A silver coin that never spends lies at every crossroads. Pick it up, and the road will offer you a shortcut — but the coin will reappear in your pocket at the next junction, heavier. In Obishaal, the coin is warm and pulses like a heartbeat.

lore_echoes.title: The Gray Wanderer's Grimoire
lore_echoes.description: Psions call the Ways Between 'the Stair.' They climb it in their dreams, trading memories for glimpses of paths not yet walked. Some never wake. The Gray Wanderer claims that the Stair is Ikasha's spine.

superstitions.name: Bread to the Stones
superstitions.effect: Crumble a crust at the base of a waystone. Ignore the first Waymark Lies penalty.

superstitions.name: Knot the Path
superstitions.effect: Tie a single knot in a piece of string and hang it from a milestone. Cancel Path Split or take −1 die on your next navigation roll (your choice).

superstitions.name: Name to the Crossroads
superstitions.effect: Whisper a dead traveler's name into the center stone. Gain +1 Effect when bargaining with a Toll-Taker this scene, but mark Obligation to the Wayfinder.

minor_complications: **Exposure:** Your actions draw unwanted attention from path keepers or wayward spirits.
**Noise:** Sounds of your actions alert nearby travelers or memory echoes.
**Trace:** Evidence of your passage marks your route for trackers or reflection points.
**Delay:** A brief but meaningful setback costs you time or favorable path alignment.
**Supply Strain:** Mark +1 segment on a relevant resource timer.
moderate_setbacks: **Alarm Raised:** Toll-taker or wayward guide becomes aware and begins responding.
**Position Lost:** You lose advantageous ground/cover/stealth due to path shift or reality thinning.
**Foe Appears:** A memory-thief or forbidden path entity arrives on scene.
**Gear Trouble:** A piece of equipment becomes Compromised/Neglected.
**Lock/Barrier:** A simple obstacle now requires a test to overcome.
serious_trouble: **Reinforcements:** Additional wayward spirits, path entities, or alternate selves arrive.
**Key Gear Breaks:** A crucial tool/weapon becomes temporarily unusable.
**Major Twist:** The situation fundamentally changes — path loops/time shifts/reality fractures.
**Rail Tick:** Advance a relevant campaign/front timer by 1 segment.
**Condition Applied:** Mark Fatigue 1/Harm 1/Condition appropriate to fiction.
major_turns: **Trap Springs:** A prepared danger activates with full effect.
**Authority Arrival:** The Wayfinder, Dead-Road Keeper, or Road's Child intervenes.
**Scene Shift:** The environment changes dramatically — reality thins/paths converge/time loops.
**Patron Omen:** Divine/arcane forces take notice — omen appears/blessing lost/curse manifests.
**Narrative Pivot:** The story takes an unexpected turn that reframes objectives.
region_specific: **Obishaal (Dream-Logic):** Paths rearrange without warning, reflections speak unbidden, destinations shift mid-journey. A character may hear Ikasha's whisper as a free omen (the GM may spend 1 SB to make it a false omen).

**Obishaal (Memory Currency):** Memories become tangible, forgotten knowledge resurfaces, past and present blur. Trading a memory here may also tick the Virtue or Vice timer depending on the memory's nature.

**Obishaal (Virtue and Vice):** Decisions echo forward, alternate selves appear, paths judge moral weight. The GM may spend SB to force a character to test a virtue or offer a vice that ticks their Vice timer.

path_moves_and_procedures.weighing_of_steps: When the company enters a liminal path (Mist-Ford, Bone Corridor, etc.), choose one: **Pay the Toll** (each PC names a small truth or a fond memory; GM banks 1 SB, +1 Position on navigation); **Refuse the Toll** (+1d on Speed, but start a Way-Scale [4] timer); **Bargain the Toll** (trade a Diamond reward as if it were a memory; cancel one imminent Club card in this scene). When Way-Scale fills, trigger Crossroads Judgment at the next junction.
path_moves_and_procedures.reflection_duel: When confronted by an alternate self or Reflection Point, state what that self wants from you and roll your best social action. **Success:** gain a Guide-Light tag for the scene and clear 1 tick from Paths Decide. **Mixed:** trade places for one exchange or take a Condition: Disoriented. **Miss:** the reflection walks away with one of your Diamonds (GM picks the most narratively apt).

memory_exchange_table.memory_offered: A childhood smell, a forgotten nickname
memory_exchange_table.side_effect: A familiar place feels strange for a scene

memory_exchange_table.memory_offered: A first failure or small betrayal
memory_exchange_table.side_effect: You gain a tell (the Ways recognize you)

memory_exchange_table.memory_offered: A true fear you have never spoken
memory_exchange_table.side_effect: A dream pursues you for 1–3 nights

memory_exchange_table.memory_offered: The details of a kept promise
memory_exchange_table.side_effect: An NPC tied to that promise misremembers you

memory_exchange_table.buys: Convert one Club into Trace only
memory_exchange_table.side_effect: The scar 'moves' (cosmetic) until the next dawn

memory_exchange_table.buys: Treat the next Heart face as an ally

path_moves_and_procedures.exchange_rule: If you pay the same kind of memory twice in a journey, start Hollowing [4]. When it fills, you gain the Backwards Pilgrim tag until you reclaim what was lost.

way_keys_and_taboos_d6: Speak Last: Only the final word said at a gate is true; others are 'practice.' First speakers take −1d on their next test.
Step Odd: Crossings require an odd number of steps; even counts loop you back one scene.
Name Nothing: True names wake Name-Theft; use titles or lose a Diamond.
Wet Iron: A drop of water on iron cancels one glamour once per scene.
Back Gift: Leave something behind to go forward; refuse and tick Way-Scale.
Answer Bent: Answer a waystone's question with a metaphor, not a fact, or trigger Truth Payment.

boss_archetypes.name: The Archivist of Unmade Roads
boss_archetypes.description: A cloak stitched from surveyor's cords — the keeper of every road never taken.
cracks: a Choice Compass reveals the true path

boss_archetypes.name: The Toll-Matriarch Beneath the Bridge
boss_archetypes.description: Many hands, one voice like wet stone — she collects what is owed.
cracks: a Passage Token marks you as belonging
a Road's Name commands her to stand aside

boss_archetypes.name: The Wayfinder's Shadow
boss_archetypes.description: Your silhouette, two steps ahead — a decision that has already been made without you.
cracks: a Grace Passage slips past its gaze

boss_archetypes.name: Ikasha's Nightmare (Dream-Eater)
boss_archetypes.description: Appears only in the deepest layer — the hunger beneath the sleeping goddess.
cracks: a filled Virtue timer can be spent to reject the nightmare
a memory of true self-sacrifice (cost 1 permanent Bond) banishes it entirely

encounter_seeds.title: The Promise Bridge's Receipt
encounter_seeds.description: An old vow you never spoke was logged here. To cross, define when you would have sworn it — and to whom.

encounter_seeds.title: Thirteenth Stone Auction
encounter_seeds.description: The stone sells three possible endings. Each bidder is you from a different failure.

encounter_seeds.title: Bone Corridor Choir
encounter_seeds.description: Shadows sing a name wrong by one letter. Correct it and gain Truth-Compass; ignore it and start Name-Theft.

encounter_seeds.title: Ikasha's Finger Bone
encounter_seeds.description: A character finds a bone that pulses with dream-light. If they hold it while sleeping, they can speak to Ikasha directly — but each time, the Waking Dream timer ticks.

extensions.choice_dial: **Resolve High:** +1 Position on Path Split tests; the first Dream-Bleed each session hits harder (start at 2). **Drift High:** +1 Effect when bargaining with way-entities; the first Truth Payment each session costs a cherished detail. Center the Dial by naming aloud the next choice and why you might refuse it; clear 1 tick from Way-Scale.
extensions.counter_seal: Once per scene, if justified: break a single metaphysical instruction (taboo, key, or omen) by presenting a memory in symbol form (a token, a letter, a sketch). Gain +1d on that crossing; the GM banks 1 SB as a Marked Consequence to spend when reflections return.
start_of_scene_murmurs_d6: Second Sunrise: light arrives twice; your first missed navigation roll becomes a mixed success.
Name Draft: the air steals a syllable; your next lie sounds true once.
Echo Scale: your footprints owe a step — skip a square or tick Way-Scale +1.
Pale Bell: time hiccups; the first Club can be delayed until the end of the scene.
Traveler's Chorus: distant voices agree with you; +1d on appeals to path entities.
Hollow Weather: rain that does not wet; conditions look dire but impose no penalties this scene.
plugin_sb_conversions: 1 SB → Footprint Vote: your tracks choose a different direction; increase DV by 1 on any roll that relies on following a trail.
2 SB → Echo of Refusal: a choice you avoided manifests as a minor obstacle (a locked gate, a forgotten toll). If the choice involved a vice, also tick the Vice timer of the character who refused.

3+ SB → Threshold Cracks: the path fractures; gain a temporary Path-Cutter effect but start Convergence [4] (all travelers you have met will arrive together at the next junction). Additionally, Ikasha's dream seeps through the cracks; each character hears a single word of her voice.
cross_regional_conversions: **Valewood:** Road's Name may count as a Valeheart Clause once if spoken under leaves; doing so creates Court Tithe [2].
**Mistlands:** Grace Passage functions as Pall Indulgence over one levee crown at night; ring a bell afterward or start Witchlight Count.
**Vhasia:** Way-Wisdom can be presented as 'pilgrim right' to bypass one Interdict barrier; begin a Parlement Divided tick.
**Viterra:** Passage Token can be notarized into a temporary Ferry Priority; on use, advance Border-Lace.
**Ubral:** Memory-Anchor counts as a Guest-Token at one hearth if you recount a family road-tale.
**Silkstrand:** Path-Cutter doubles as a night-boat route once; spend 1 favor with a smuggler or trigger Seal Counterfeit.
**Linn:** Choice Compass acts as a Pilot's Token in a reed-maze if you pay a name to the water.
**Theona:** Crossroads Boon allows counting 'eight-and-one' to cross an Uncounted Bridge safely once.

patronage_and_power: In Obishaal, power flows through understanding the metaphysical nature of dreams, the ability to navigate virtue and vice, and the careful management of one's weight before the scales. The true authorities are those who know the True Names of dream-layers, can mediate between the living and the Unsettled, and understand the currency of virtue. **For the GM:** Patronage in Obishaal revolves around guidance, safe passage, and the ability to navigate moral tests. Rewards often take the form of dream-tokens, fragments of Ikasha's memory, or knowledge of a layer's True Name. Tie rewards to visible symbols (compasses, anchors, bells) that can be challenged, stolen, or voided by the dream itself. Let rival guides (Virtue vs. Vice) issue conflicting directions, forcing players to choose whose favor matters more. Use the crossroads, waystations, and dream-layers as arenas for moral contests, where a single act of mercy can ascend you — and a single act of cruelty can damn you. In Obishaal, your virtue is your power, and your power determines whether you wake or sleep forever.
